newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Andean pact waits on Peru before Mercosur talks.
newsitem.headline: Andean pact waits on Peru before Mercosur talks.

text.p: Andean pact countries have postponed until March trade talks with South America's largest customs bloc, Mercosur, to allow lapsed Andean member Peru time to reconsider the terms under which it might return to the pact, trade ministers said.
Peru excluded itself from the trade pact, which also groups Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Bolivia, in 1992 after disagreeing with proposed tariff schedules.

"The return will be progressive, it doesn't have to be from one day to another," Peruvian trade minister, Gustavo Caillaux, told reporters outside the Caracas-based headquarters of the Andean Development Corporation.
"But if we didn't want to return, I'd still be at home."

After Peru's 45-day deadline expires, pact members will begin technical negotiations with Mercosur members -- Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay -- on a possible trade group that could one day span South America, Venezuelan development minister Freddy Rojas Parra said.
"Come March we'll be readying ourselves for the Mercosur talks," he said.

The negotiations, previously scheduled for February, will center on common general trade rules, including procedures for the dispute resolution, clauses to protect domestic industry and a general outline for the reduction of tariffs.
